newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates rise on low supplies.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates rise on low supplies.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates rose on Tuesday on low supplies and higher demand from spinners, brokers at the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said.
In the kerb market the rate for NIAB-78 rose to 2,725 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), including 10 percent sales tax, from Monday's 2,700, broker Nasim Usman said.
Rates rose as spinners, who had used up their stocks in August, returned to the market, Usman said. Prices were likely to open mixed on Wednesday, he added.

The KCA said exports had reached 1.82 million 375-lb bales by August 25 since the 1995/96 season began on September 1, 1995. Dealers had registered 2.33 million bales for export with the state-run Export Promotion Bureau by June 3, it said.
